Auto-summary (auto-gen): Walkthrough of Console usage analytics and per-route cost breakdown. Focus on how to attribute token spend to product routes, set alerts, and auto-fallback policies for Dedicated vs Hosted. Action items captured.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll do a quick intro, then rafael will drive the console walkthrough. just want to confirm agenda — usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown and then q&a.
[00:18] Sonia Patel: Sounds good, thanks. we're mostly interested in being able to see per-feature cost, like search vs chat, and export that to our billing system.
[00:28] Rafael Ortiz: Great — i'll share my screen. so first screen is the high-level usage view, you can see tokens in last 30 days, requests per minute, latency p95. we ingest routes tagged from your api keys or route names.
[00:42] Marcus Lee: Quick Q — how do you map our internal routes to the console? we have route names in our API gateway.
[00:50] Rafael Ortiz: we support route tag propagation in the sdk and also via header X-Redwood-Route. if that's not possible you can do a join on request_id in the logs. occasionally the agent mis-parses route names in the auto ingest so you might see a "route_unk" for the first few days.
[01:10] Lena Park: (screen narration) here's the per-route dashboard, each card shows tokens, avg token length, cost per 1k tokens, and the model used. you can filter by model family, region, and deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private).
[01:32] Dana Ruiz: I see a bucket called "inference-chat" and another "prod-search" — is that coming from our route names?
[01:38] Rafael Ortiz: yes those are route names. you can also add metadata tags — environment:prod or team:search — those show up in the dashboard and in exported csvs.
[01:50] Sonia Patel: On cost breakdown — curious how you calculate unit costs when we use different model variants and quantizations across deployments.
[01:58] Rafael Ortiz: good question. the console maintains a cost model per deployment: it factors gpu-hour, kernel selection (intel vs nvidia), quantization multiplier, and batching efficiency. then it attributes cost down to routes using token-weighted attribution. so if your search route uses gpt-small-quant at 200 tokens average and chat uses gpt-medium with 800 tokens, the per-route cost reflects that.
[02:24] Marcus Lee: Does that model account for caching and prefix reuse? our search has a lot of prefix hits.
[02:30] Rafael Ortiz: yes — we instrument prefix/KV cache hits and apply savings as a negative cost line item. sometimes the transcript tool writes KV "cash" but it's KV cache in the console.
[02:44] Sonia Patel: Nice. we need to show cost per feature to our finance team and create alerts if a route spikes beyond a threshold.
[02:52] Lena Park: Alerts are configurable — threshold by tokens, cost, or request rate. you can send to slack, webhook, or paging tools. also can set anomaly detection for unusual token per-request growth.
[03:08] Marcus Lee: On the hosted vs dedicated question — if we move heavy routes to dedicated, will the console show blended costs?
[03:15] Rafael Ortiz: yes you get both per-deployment and blended views. dedicated shows reserved capacity amortized over the commit period; hosted shows per-token variable cost. the console will show potential savings by simulating dedicated commitments given your traffic profile — that's the Optimize integration.
[03:32] Sonia Patel: How accurate is the simulation? finance wants a percent error estimate.
[03:36] Rafael Ortiz: typically within 8-12% for steady-state traffic. for spiky workloads error can be larger; we recommend a two-week benchmark run on dedicated to validate the numbers in your environment.
[03:50] Dana Ruiz: Security checks — where do we get audit logs and is there SSO support?
[03:56] Maya Chen: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. audit logs are exportable to your SIEM as json and you can keep them in your private bucket for residency. retina — i mean redwood console supports retention configs per org.
[04:14] Sonia Patel: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO certs?
[04:16] Maya Chen: yes, SOC 2 Type II in our security pack. i'll share the security dossier after the call, including KMS/HSM integrations and the private deployment options for stricter data controls.
[04:28] Marcus Lee: About private deployments — if we go private on prem, do we still get the same console features?
[04:34] Rafael Ortiz: Private control plane has parity for usage analytics and the per-route dashboards; some telemetry routes require a connector but the UI is the same. there are a few admin-only features that are cloud-managed in hosted but available as an addon for private.
[04:50] Sonia Patel: Great. can you show an example export?
[04:53] Lena Park: exporting now — csv includes columns: timestamp, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate, deployment, region, tags. you can also push to BigQuery or Snowflake with a sync connector.
[05:12] Marcus Lee: we use BigQuery — nice. how frequent is the sync?
[05:15] Rafael Ortiz: near-real-time with minutes granularity; for billing exports we do hourly rollups.
[05:22] Sonia Patel: There was earlier a mention of per-token discounts and tiering — how does Redwood apply committed discounts?
[05:29] Maya Chen: committed capacity is applied as a separate billing line. the console will show both discounted unit price and the effective blended cost when you include reserved amortization. we also surface effective cpms and per-1000 token rates in the UI.
[05:44] Dana Ruiz: Any limitations on model variants for Dedicated? we want to run a quantized 4-bit model and some fp16.
[05:50] Rafael Ortiz: Dedicated pools support fp16 and quantized models; some older kernels have quirks, but we ship kernel selection logic that picks best kernels per model. in rare cases we fallback to a compatible variant and mark it in the route timeline.
[06:06] Sonia Patel: Can we tag requests with product identifiers so finance can attribute to P&L?
[06:10] Rafael Ortiz: yes, route tags and metadata are the supported pattern. you can also send a billing_tag header and we'll show that in the billing export.
[06:20] (brief cross talk)
[06:28] Marcus Lee: Let's talk about the benchmark you suggested — what data do you need from our side?
[06:32] Rafael Ortiz: sample traffic profile, typical prompt/response sizes, expected concurrency, and a small test dataset for correctness checks. we'll run for two weeks on the dedicated pool to capture seasonality.
[06:44] Sonia Patel: Who will manage the dedicated environment? our infra team or Redwood?
[06:48] Maya Chen: managed dedicated has Redwood ops and customer infra in a shared model; for fully private deployments customer manages infra but we provide the control plane and runbooks.
[06:59] Dana Ruiz: Timeline — if we greenlight pilot next week how long to stand up dedicated for the benchmark?
[07:03] Rafael Ortiz: typically 3-5 business days once we have onboarding info and commit to a minimal reserved size.
[07:10] Sonia Patel: Risk/objection — our legal asks about data residency and auditability for EU customers.
[07:16] Maya Chen: we have region pinning and can keep EU traffic within eu-west clouds. audit logs and access logs can be routed to your EU bucket via our connector. i'll attach the security docs.
[07:28] Marcus Lee: Any hidden costs we should be aware of? cross-region egress or large cache storage?
[07:34] Rafael Ortiz: cross-region egress follows cloud provider pricing; we surface it as part of the cost simulation. cache storage is usually small compared to token costs but if you retain large KV caches across many keys we can show estimates in the Optimize recommendations.
[07:50] (screen scrubbing)
[07:56] Lena Park: switching to Optimize tab — here you'll see suggested batching, quantization profiles, and routes we recommend for dedicated. these recommendations are workload-specific and show estimated monthly savings.
[08:12] Sonia Patel: Can we export those recommendations to a ticketing system?
[08:15] Rafael Ortiz: yes export as csv or push to Jira via webhook.
[08:20] Dana Ruiz: I'm going to note down the immediate follow-ups.

[08:55] Sonia Patel: Can you also include an example billing export for a month so our FP&A can see format?
